description:
Publish source as an app: a process Valet builds from your files and runs behind its own URL. Use it when the work needs a server, a background process, or a database. A Procfile at the root says how to start each process type; the web type serves the app's URL and must listen on $PORT, which Valet sets. Node, Python, and Go are supported. Apply the governance skill before calling.

title and description are required with files and a call missing either is refused: Valet writes the app's valet.yaml from them. files carries text only: source, Procfile, configuration, and a manifest the build installs from (package.json, requirements.txt, or go.mod), never installed packages. When you can run git with network access, or the app is large or holds binary files, call create_push, push, and pass push: {id, commit} instead; the commit supplies its own valet.yaml. Pass files or push, not both.

Create the app first with create_service (kind: app), then publish to its name. Publishing replaces the app's source, so read get_source first when the app is not yours. Returns a build id: poll get_build every ten to fifteen seconds until deploy_state is up, crashed, or refused, and between polls tell the person what its phase says the build is doing. A succeeded build is not live until its processes start, and on crashed a web process keeps serving its last release, so a working URL does not prove the new release is live. Read each crashed process's state_reason, fix the app or the failure it names, and publish again.

Write the app to start without its variables and resources and serve a page saying what is missing, never exiting. Then attach_resource, which takes the app's own variables too, applies both in one restart; set_env_vars restarts it with variables alone. A new app is private: only members of the organization that owns it can open it, after signing in to Valet. Use set_service_access to make it public or password-protected. Requires connecting a Valet account.

description.description: Required with files. One sentence saying what the app does.

discard_draft.description: Set true to discard an open draft on this app that another session left. Omit to be told about it instead. Not used with push.

files.description: Required unless push is given. The app's files, [{path, content}]. A Procfile at the root is required.

content.description: Required. The file's complete text content.

path.description: Required. The file's path, relative to the app root.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of starting a second build. Use a new key for new files: a repeated key returns the earlier result even when the files changed.

name.description: Required. The app's name, which is the first label of its URL. The app must exist: create it first with create_service. Publishing to it replaces its source.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to publish into. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

push.description: Publish a Git push instead of files: the id create_push returned and the commit you pushed to its branch. Use it when you can run git with network access, because it sends only what changed. Pass files or push, not both; every other argument keeps its meaning.

commit.description: Required. The full sha of the commit you pushed to the push's branch. The recipe create_push returned prints it.

title.description: Required with files. What the app is called, written for a person.

name: publish_app
title: Publish an app
